finding.claim: update_doc computes can_edit(g.user, doc) but discards the result, so any caller reaching PUT /doc/<doc_id> can overwrite the body of any document regardless of ownership or editor membership.
finding.source: doc_id path segment (docs.py:17) and JSON body field request.json['body'] (docs.py:20) supplied by the HTTP client; the caller's identity is g.user, set by auth code outside this repo.
finding.sink: doc['body'] assignment at docs.py:20 (persisted stored document content).

trace.note: doc = DOCS[doc_id] loads the target document.
can_edit(g.user, doc) is called but its boolean return is ignored; no abort.
Sibling update_title calls require_edit(g.user, doc), which aborts with 403; update_doc does not.

finding.guards_checked: can_edit (docs.py:7-8) is correct but not enforced on this path; require_edit (docs.py:11-13) is not called in update_doc; no before_request hook, decorator, or other g.user usage exists in the repo (grep confirmed). Precondition: caller must pass external auth that sets g.user; if g.user is unset the request 500s instead of bypassing.

verdict.guard_found: can_edit at docs.py:7-8 returns a bool, but update_doc calls it as a bare statement at docs.py:19 and never tests the result. require_edit (docs.py:11-13) aborts with 403 but is not called in update_doc. The sibling update_title at docs.py:27 does call require_edit. No before_request hook or decorator exists in docs.py, and the glob shows no other files in the repo.
verdict.reason: update_doc at docs.py:19 discards the boolean from can_edit, so the write at docs.py:20 runs for any authenticated caller who can reach PUT /doc/<doc_id>, while the sibling update_title at docs.py:27 correctly aborts via require_edit. The attacker only needs a low-privilege authenticated session, and no effective control blocks the overwrite.
